The game was going well for me until move 36. I was a knight up at one point and had won the c7 pawn. Then I played Rc6 to attack h6 without noticing that the b7 pawn could capture on c6. After bxc6 I was a rook down for a pawn, with no realistic counterplay, so I resigned.

I've rewritten my strategy brain (version 3). The main new rule is to check, before every rook move, whether an enemy pawn or piece can capture on the destination square.

args.text:
1. Develop, castle early, control the centre.
2. Before every move, list enemy attackers and my defenders of each piece and pawn I touch, including pawn recaptures and long diagonals.
3. Count attackers vs defenders; add defenders rather than let a pawn drop.
4. Before a queen move, check whether the destination is attacked by a pawn or minor piece.
5. Never recapture with the queen into a rook's line if a minor piece recapture exists.
6. Prefer solid moves over speculative sacrifices.
7. When ahead, trade pieces, keep the king safe, convert simply.
8. Grab undefended enemy pieces after confirming no recapture.
9. Watch knight forks on c2/d3.
10. NEW: Before a knight move, check enemy pawn attacks (game 2: Nd4 lost to c3xd4).
11. NEW: Before a rook move, check knight and pawn attacks on the target.
12. NEW: When down material, avoid rook trades into bare-pawn endings.
